'''Victor Wembanyama''' (born 4 January 2004) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for [[Metropolitans 92]]<!-- DO NOT CHANGE THIS UNTIL THE NBA DRAFT ACTUALLY OCCURS --> of the [[LNB Pro A]]. He is widely projected to be selected [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall]] in the [[2023 NBA draft]] and is considered one of the greatest basketball prospects of his generation.

Born in [[Le Chesnay]], France, Wembanyama began his professional career with [[Nanterre 92]] of the LNB Pro A in 2019. Two years later, he moved to [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL]] and won the Pro A title in his only season with the team. In the [[2022–23 Pro A season|2022–23 season]], Wembanyama signed with Metropolitans 92 and became the youngest player to win the [[LNB Pro A MVP|Pro A MVP]] award, while earning [[LNB Pro A Best Defender|Pro A Best Defender]] honors and leading the league in scoring, rebounds and [[block (basketball)|blocks]]. He has been named an [[LNB All-Star]] twice, winning All-Star Game MVP once, and is a three-time [[LNB Pro A Best Young Player|Pro A Best Young Player]].

Wembanyama plays for the [[France men's national basketball team|French national basketball team]]. At the youth level, he has led his team to two silver medals, including at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]], where he set the [[FIBA]] record for blocks per game in a single tournament.

==Professional career==
===Nanterre 92 (2019–2021)===
In the 2019–20 season, Wembanyama gained his first professional experience with the [[Nanterre 92]] senior team under head coach [[Pascal Donnadieu]],<ref name=jaquin/> receiving limited playing time in two games.<ref name=realgm/> He primarily competed in LNB Espoirs, the French under-21 league, and also played for the under-18 team.<ref name=jaquin/><ref>{{cite web |title=Nanterre : Victor Wembanyama dans le groupe professionnel contre Orléans |url=https://www.bebasket.fr/nanterre-victor-wembanyama-dans-le-groupe-professionnel-contre-orleans/ |publisher=BeBasket |access-date=8 January 2023 |language=fr |date=26 October 2019}}</ref> Wembanyama made his professional debut on 29 October 2019, playing 31 seconds against [[Pallacanestro Brescia|Brescia]] in the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. At 15 years, nine months and 25 days old, he was the second-youngest player after Stefan Petković to play in the EuroCup.<ref>{{cite news |last=Lupo |first=Nicola |title=Nanterre: il 15enne Victor Wembanyama fa il suo debutto in EuroCup contro Brescia |url=https://sportando.basketball/nanterre-il-15enne-victor-wembanyama-fa-il-suo-debutto-in-eurocup-contro-brescia/ |newspaper=Sportando |access-date=11 January 2023 |language=Italian |date=29 October 2019}}</ref> In February 2020, Wembanyama played for Nanterre's under-18 team at the [[2019–20 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament#Kaunas, Lithuania|Kaunas qualifying tournament]] for the [[2019–20 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Adidas Next Generation Tournament]] (ANGT). On 8 February, he posted 22 [[point (basketball)|points]], 15 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and an ANGT-record nine blocks in a win over the under-18 team of [[Basket Zaragoza|Zaragoza]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Victor Wembanyama, 16, has historic ANGT performance |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1019678/victor-wembanyama-16-has-historic-angt-performance/ |publisher=Eurohoops |access-date=8 February 2020 |date=8 February 2020}}</ref> Wembanyama averaged 15.8 points, 12 rebounds, 2.8 [[steal (basketball)|steals]], and six blocks per game in Kaunas, leading the tournament in blocks and earning all-tournament team honours.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hein |first=David |title=Tubelis takes home MVP as Rytas takes first place |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/adpcfgrt5nl3cg8p/tubelis-takes-home-mvp-as-rytas-takes-first-place |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |access-date=18 October 2020 |date=9 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201018232953/https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/adpcfgrt5nl3cg8p/tubelis-takes-home-mvp-as-rytas-takes-first-place |archive-date= 18 October 2020}}</ref> He finished the Espoirs season averaging 10.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 3.3 blocks per game, mostly coming off the bench.<ref name="lnb">{{cite web |title=Victor Wembanyama |url=https://www.lnb.fr/elite/joueur/?id=8052 |publisher=[[Ligue nationale de basket]] |access-date=4 January 2023 |language=fr}}</ref> 

In the 2020–21 season, Wembanyama split time between Nanterre's senior and under-21 teams and signed an agreement to also play for [[Centre Fédéral de Basket-ball|Centre Fédéral]] in the [[Nationale Masculine 1]] (NM1).<ref>{{cite web |last=Bosi |first=Kévin |title=Victor Wembanyama évoluera aussi au Pôle France |url=https://www.ffbb.com/pole-france-basket/victor-wembanyama-evoluera-aussi-au-pole-france |publisher=[[French Federation of Basketball]] |access-date=10 January 2023 |language=fr |date=10 September 2020}}</ref> On 23 September 2020, he made his [[LNB Pro A]] debut, grabbing one rebound in four minutes against [[JL Bourg]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Rutard |first=Sacha |title=Le chiffre: Victor Wembanyama, 16 ans, 8 mois et 20 jours |url=https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/518095/le-chiffre-victor-wembanyama-16-ans-8-mois-et-20-jours/ |publisher=Basket Europe |access-date=18 October 2020 |language=fr |date=24 September 2020}}</ref> In October, Wembanyama featured in a [[viral video]] where he showcased his skills in a two-on-two [[pick-up game]] against [[Rudy Gobert]] and [[Vincent Poirier]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Faucha |first=Fernando |title=Victor Wembanyama, el gigante francés que tiene loca a la NBA |url=https://as.com/baloncesto/2020/10/22/mas_baloncesto/1603354169_364517.html |website=[[Diario AS]] |access-date=12 January 2023 |language=Spanish |date=22 October 2020}}</ref> On 12 December, he suffered a [[stress fracture]] in his [[fibula]] during an Espoirs game against [[BCM Gravelines-Dunkerque]], with an estimated recovery time of eight weeks. Wembanyama was sidelined from the [[2020–21 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament#Valencia, Spain|Valencia qualifying tournament]] for the ANGT.<ref>{{cite web |title=Victor Wembanyama |website=[[L'Équipe]] |access-date=12 January 2023 |language=fr |date=16 December 2020}}</ref> After missing two and a half months with injury, he began receiving more playing time with the senior |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Victor-Wembanyama/Summary/136048 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=11 January 2023}}</ref> Following the season, he opted to leave Nanterre.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Pruneta|first=Laurent|date=18 June 2021|title=Basket : le phénomène Victor Wembanyama quitte [[File:Victor Wembanyama Mets 92 (2).jpg|thumb|upright|200px|Wembanyama with [[Metropolitans 92]] in 2022]]

== National team career ==
=== Junior national team ===
Wembanyama represented [[France men's national under-17 basketball team|France]] at the [[2019 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Udine]], Italy. In an 80–78 quarterfinal win over [[Croatia men's national under-16 and under-17 basketball team|Croatia]], he recorded 12 points, 21 rebounds and eight blocks.<ref>{{cite web |last=Rutard |first=Sacha |title=Euro U16: Propulsée par un phénoménal Victor Wembanyama (37 d'évaluation), la France se hisse en demi-finale |url=https://www.basketeurope.com/une/472148/euro-u16-propulse-par-un-phenomenal-victor-wembanyama-37-devaluation-la-france-se-hisse-en-demi-finale/ |publisher=Basket Europe |access-date=9 February 2020 |language=fr |date=14 August 2019}}</ref> He averaged nine points, 9.6 rebounds and a tournament-leading 5.3 blocks per game, leading France to a silver medal and earning all-tournament team honours.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2019/team/France|title=France at the FIBA U16 European Championship 2019|publisher=[[FIBA]] |language=en|access-date=30 October 2019}}</ref>

He then competed at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]] in [[Latvia]]. Wembanyama averaged 14 points, 7.4 rebounds and 5.7 blocks per game, and was named to the all-tournament team after leading France to the silver medal. He recorded 22 points, eight rebounds and eight blocks in an 83–81 loss to the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chet Holmgren takes home TISSOT MVP award after helping USA to U19 World Cup title |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2021/news/chet-holmgren-takes-home-tissot-mvp-award-after-helping-usa-to-u19-world-cup-title |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=12 July 2021 |date=11 July 2021}}</ref> Wembanyama set the FIBA record for blocks per game in a single tournament.<ref>{{cite web |last=Rutard |first=Sacha |title=Victor Wembanyama a battu, à la Coupe du Monde U19, le record de contres pour un évènement FIBA ! |url=https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/558149/victor-wembanyama-a-battu-a-la-coupe-du-monde-u19-le-record-de-contres-pour-un-evenement-fiba/ |publisher=Basket Europe |language=fr |access-date=23 August 2021 |date=17 July 2021}}</ref>

=== Senior national team ===
Wembanyama was on the preliminary 17-man roster of the [[France men's national basketball team|French national team]] for [[EuroBasket 2022]], but was ruled out a month ahead, due to an injury he suffered at the end of the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |title=France's Victor Wembanyama ruled out of EuroBasket 2022 due to injury |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/07/30/france-victor-wembanyama-eurobasket-2022-injury/ |publisher=The Rookie Wire |access-date=15 January 2023 |date=30 July 2022}}</ref> He was selected again for the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe) – Qualifiers|World Cup qualifiers]] in November.<ref>{{cite web |title=Victor Wembanyama to join France for World Cup qualifiers |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/34748943 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=15 January 2023 |date=7 October 2022}}</ref> In his debut with the senior team, on 11 November 2022, he scored 20 points and grabbed nine rebounds in a 90–65 win over [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuania]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Victor Wembanyama debut: 20-point near double-double against Lithuania |url=https://basketnews.com/news-180757-victor-wembanyama-debut-20-point-near-double-double-against-lithuania.html |publisher=Basketnews |access-date=15 January 2023 |date=11 November 2022}}</ref>

==Off the court==
[[File:Victor Wembanyama NBA Paris Game.jpg|thumb|upright|Wembanyama sitting courtside at an [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] game in [[Paris]] in 2023]]
Wembanyama is represented by [[sports agent|agent]] Bouna Ndiaye of Comsport. His family has a longtime relationship with Ndiaye, whose son was coached by Wembanyama's mother from an early age. Ndiaye advised Wembanyama by the time he was 15 years old and signed him as a client in 2022.<ref name="mullen">{{cite web |last=Mullen |first=Liz |title=Labor and Agents: French Connection: How agent for projected top NBA Draft pick built his practice |url=https://www.sportsbusinessjournal.com/Journal/Issues/2023/01/09/Insiders/labor-and-agents.aspx |website=Sports Business Journal |access-date=16 January 2023 |date=9 January 2023}}</ref>

Wembanyama was a year ahead for his age in school and attended [[Secondary education in France#Lycée|lycée]] in agreement with Nanterre 92. He earned his ''[[baccalauréat]]'' with honours, specialising in earth and life sciences and social and economic sciences.<ref name=jaquin/><ref>{{cite web |last=Bertrande |first=Arnaud |title=Victor Wembanyama (ASVEL) : « Je dois devenir un joueur dominant » |url=https://www.lequotidiendusport.fr/victor-wembanyama-asvel-je-dois-devenir-un-joueur-dominant/ |website=Le Quotidien du Sport |access-date=8 January 2023 |language=fr |date=22 October 2021}}</ref>
